patterns: Round-1 (invented framing sentences) and round-2 problems (dropped hedges S023/S044, added causal or evaluative words, S028 and S094 attribution shifts, S069 and S076 sense changes) do not recur: hedges are kept, attributions run through the editors, Black, Allen, Howlett, the translators, and Dionysius, Aquinas and Gregory only through a scholar or through Pico. Remaining problems are small: S094 adds an uncited fact about Howlett's note; S085 adds 'the tradition Pico draws on'; S047 and S049 leave the reporter unnamed against S002/S040's own rule. No Aquinas, Scotus or Dionysius claim stands in the essay's own voice.
